newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IMF urges action on SAfrica macro-economic plan.
newsitem.headline: IMF urges action on SAfrica macro-economic plan.

text.p: The IMF would not impose any additional conditions on its balance of payments support for South Africa as long as the government's macro-economic growth strategy was credibly implemented, executive director Michel Camdessus said on Friday.
Addressing the parliamentary finance committee, Camdessus pledged support "in as much as you would require it, and in as much as you would need our support".
This would involve replenishing "your exchange reserves and to provide you with our financing if it appears to your government desirable".
He said that although several steps had been taken to deal with South Africa's economic problems, including unemployment, more decisive and credible action was necessary.
In particular, fiscal and monetary policy needed attention to halt market pressure, he said.
He said he believed the macro-economic strategy was "a good strategy".

"I am possibly only a little too impatient to see the government substantiating (it), after proper consultation with its partners, and then having this policy producing possibly even earlier results than those that are indicated."
"The world needs your success much more than possibly South Africa believes," he said.
Camdessus was scheduled to hold a press conference with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel at 1530 GMT.
